[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Per the Wikipedia article on 33 Thomas Street, this New York City building (also known as the AT&T Long Lines Building) sits on the east side of Church Street between Thomas and Worth Streets in Tribeca, Lower Manhattan. It is 550 feet tall with 29 floors and was built from 1969 to 1974 as a telephone exchange facility housing long distance switching equipment, designed for self sufficiency with independent gas and water supplies and protection from nuclear fallout. The article states it currently operates telephone switching equipment and secure data centers, and reports that journalists have documented it as housing an NSA surveillance hub, a claim this session did not independently verify. This is a Wikipedia article, not an AT&T publication; no square footage or power capacity in MW is stated.
